title: Foundation Models Meet Agriculture: Challenges Beyond Pretraining
abstract: arXiv:2608.30392v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Global food security and sustainable climate action increasingly rely on robust, scalable agricultural monitoring. Earth observation foundation models have emerged as powerful, label-efficient tools across general remote sensing domains, yet early attempts to deploy them for agricultural applications have yielded surprisingly poor results. We hypothesize that this performance gap stems from the extreme heterogeneity of agricultural landscapes and the inherent inability of current earth observation foundation models to adapt to task-specific nuances. In this work, we systematically evaluate two critical bottlenecks hindering the deployment of foundation models in agricultural tasks, benchmarking two earth observation foundation models, a foundation model designed for tabular data, and conventional supervised baselines across seven real-world agricultural datasets spanning yield prediction, phenology estimation, and crop classification. translated_title: 基础模型邂逅农业：预训练之外的挑战
translated_abstract: 全球粮食安全和可持续气候行动日益依赖于强大且可扩展的农业监测。地球观测基础模型已在通用遥感领域成为强大且标签高效的工具，然而早期将其部署于农业应用的尝试却得到了令人惊讶的糟糕结果。我们假设这一性能差距源于农业景观的极端异质性，以及当前地球观测基础模型缺乏适应任务特定细微差别的固有能力。在本工作中，我们系统地评估了阻碍基础模型在农业任务中部署的两个关键瓶颈，在七个真实世界农业数据集上对两个地球观测基础模型、一个面向表格数据的基础模型以及传统监督基线模型进行了基准测试，这些数据集涵盖产量预测、物候估计和作物分类任务。
tldr: 本研究揭示了当前地球观测基础模型在农业任务中表现不佳的根源在于农业景观的极端异质性与模型任务适应能力的缺失，并通过在七个真实农业数据集上对多种基础模型和监督基线进行系统基准测试，评估了阻碍其部署的两个关键瓶颈。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that the poor performance of Earth observation foundation models in agriculture stems from extreme landscape heterogeneity and their inability to adapt to task-specific nuances, and systematically benchmarks two critical bottlenecks across seven real-world agricultural datasets.
